newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Malaysia frees five Filipino fishermen - Manila.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia frees five Filipino fishermen - Manila.

text.p: Malaysia has released five Filipino fishermen detained for more than two weeks in Sabah, Philippine Foreign Minister Domingo Siazon said on Friday.
Siazon said he was informed of their release by Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Badawi who told Manila the five were caught fishing in Malaysian waters.

The Philippine presidential palace, quoting local police, had said the fishermen were abducted on April 14 from their village on a remote southern Philippine island by Malaysians who suspected the Filipinos of stealing their boat engines.
The palace quoted the police as saying seven residents were taken by the Malaysians.
Kuala Lumpur said only five Filipino fishermen were arrested on Malaysian waters.
Siazon told repoters the Filipinos might have drifted into Malaysian waters.
"They were fishing but did not know where they (were) because there is really no line between the borders," he said.
Philippine diplomats who went to Sabah said they found no sign of the two other Filipinos previously reported to have been taken by the Malaysians along with the five.
